expertInsight: Experience Cloud access depends on the external user’s license and the site’s sharing setup. Practice comparing sharing sets, sharing rules, and super user access for different users.

whoIsThisFor.heading: Who is the Experience Cloud Consultant exam for?

personas.label: Community builders
personas.description: You build customer or partner sites and want to confirm your Experience Cloud implementation knowledge.

personas.label: Consultants
personas.description: You deliver portal projects and work with templates, sharing and site content.

personas.label: Admins specialising in external users
personas.description: You administer external-user access and need to choose licenses and sharing features that fit.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Experience Cloud Consultant Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam covers Experience Cloud site design, external-user licenses, sharing, content and administration. The right design depends on who will use the site and which records they need.
bullets: 62% passing score: moderate threshold, but the content difficulty compensates.
Licensing-heavy: expect 6-8 questions on when to use Partner Community, Customer Community, and Customer Community Plus licenses.
Sharing model for external users: sharing sets, super user access, and sharing groups are heavily tested.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Build an Experience Cloud site in a Developer Edition org and test access as an external user. Practice explaining how the sharing options differ.

examFormat.heading: Experience Cloud Consultant Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test centre. Check Salesforce’s current exam guide for delivery details and requirements.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenarios ask how to build a site for a particular audience. First identify the user type and license, then determine which content, records and site features that user needs.
bestWayToPass: Start with the visitor type, their license and the records they need.
Choose a template and site features that match the audience’s task.
Compare Sharing Sets, partner sharing and guest access by their record-access rules.
Check the current Salesforce Help for license capabilities and site settings.

certificationCard.description: This credential covers planning and implementing Experience Cloud sites for customers, partners and employees, including templates, external-user access, content and site administration. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 62% pass mark, weighted towards Administration, Setup, and Configuration (25%) and Sharing, Visibility, and Licensing (17%).

keyConcepts.h2: Experience Cloud Consultant: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Site Templates and Their Use Cases
blocks.body: Choose a site template based on the job it needs to do. Customer Service supports cases and knowledge; Partner Central supports partner processes such as deal registration. Help Center emphasizes knowledge, while Build Your Own offers more design flexibility. Compare the requirements before choosing a template.

blocks.heading: Sharing Model for External Users
blocks.body: External-user access depends on the site’s license and sharing design. Sharing Sets can grant access to records related to the external user’s Account or Contact through configured mappings. Partner sharing options and guest-user access follow different rules. Choose the mechanism that matches the user type, record relationship and required access.

blocks.heading: User Licensing: Customer, Partner, and Guest Users
blocks.body: Experience Cloud sites support authenticated external users and unauthenticated guest access, subject to the site’s configuration and user licenses. License capabilities differ, so confirm the required objects, roles and sharing features before choosing a license.

blocks.heading: Audience Targeting and Personalisation
blocks.body: Audiences group visitors by criteria such as login status or profile. You can use them to show different pages or components to different groups on the same site. Review how audience membership and page settings affect what each visitor sees.

blocks.heading: Salesforce CMS and Knowledge for Content
blocks.body: Knowledge provides support articles, such as troubleshooting steps and FAQs, that visitors can search. Salesforce CMS manages content for delivery across channels, including site banners and other structured content. Practice choosing the tool that fits the content and audience.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Experience Cloud Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: For each scenario, identify the visitor, login state, license and records that the site should expose.

blocks.heading: Choose the user model first
blocks.body: Authenticated customers, partners and guest visitors have different license and access rules.

blocks.heading: Match the sharing tool to the relationship
blocks.body: Sharing Sets use configured Account or Contact mappings. Partner and guest access use other controls.

blocks.heading: Choose a site template by task
blocks.body: Case self-service, partner deal work and knowledge browsing may call for different templates.

blocks.heading: Separate content from access
blocks.body: CMS manages content; sharing and permissions determine which records a user may access.

blocks.heading: Preview visibility as each audience
blocks.body: Check component and page visibility for the intended audience before publishing.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Consultant Certifications
nextCertsAfter.intro: After this consultant certification, you can add adjacent clouds or deepen your specialisation:

sampleQuestions.question: Which site template supports customer self-service for creating and following cases?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Customer Service is the best fit because the Customer Service template is optimised for self-service portals, it includes pre-built components for case creation, case tracking, Knowledge article search, and community discussion.
whyWrong: Build Your Own is not the best choice because 'Build Your Own' requires custom development, not the purpose-built self-service case template being asked about.
Partner Central is not the best choice because partner Central is designed for partner relationship management, not general customer self-service case tracking.
Help Center is not the best choice because help Center is more focused on knowledge/FAQ browsing than the case submission/tracking workflow described.

sampleQuestions.question: How does Audience Targeting personalize an Experience Cloud site?
options: Show tailored content to audience groups
Limit the site to signed-in users
sampleQuestions.explanation: Show tailored content to audience groups is the best fit because audience Targeting lets site builders define audiences (e.g., Gold Partners, UK Customers) based on criteria, then assign specific pages, components, or content variations to each audience, enabling personalised experiences without building multiple sites.
whyWrong: Configure sign-in and single sign-on is not the best choice because managing authentication/SSO is a security configuration, unrelated to Audience Targeting's content-personalization purpose.
Measure visitor traffic and engagement is not the best choice because tracking visitor analytics is a reporting function, not what Audience Targeting does.
Limit the site to signed-in users is not the best choice because restricting access to authenticated users is a security/authentication concern, not what Audience Targeting does.

sampleQuestions.question: Which sharing feature can grant external users access to records tied to their Account or Contact?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Sharing Sets is the best fit because sharing Sets grant external users (Customer Community or Partner Community licence holders) access to records that match their Account or Contact via a defined access mapping, without requiring sharing rules or roles.
whyWrong: Manual record sharing is not the best choice because manual Sharing is a one-off mechanism, not the systematic Account/Contact-based access mechanism being asked about.
Role hierarchy is not the best choice because role Hierarchy is an internal Salesforce access structure, not designed for external user access.
External Account Hierarchy is not the best choice because sharing Sets grant access based on criteria matching, not specifically Account/Contact relationship.

sampleQuestions.question: What should a site present to help customers find answers before opening a case?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Show Knowledge before case submission is the best fit because case deflection presents Knowledge Articles to users before they submit a case, suggesting solutions that may resolve the issue without agent involvement. Knowledge must be enabled and articles published to the site for deflection to work.
whyWrong: Classify incoming cases with Einstein is not the best choice because einstein Case Classification routes cases after creation, it doesn't itself deflect cases from being created.
Route emails into Salesforce is not the best choice because email-to-Case with routing is about processing submitted cases, not deflecting them before submission.
Use Web-to-Case without Knowledge is not the best choice because web-to-Case captures cases from a public form, it doesn't deflect case creation through self-service.

sampleQuestions.question: Which partner-site capability lets resellers submit and follow potential deals?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Deal Registration is the best fit because deal Registration allows channel partners to claim credit for potential deals by registering them through the partner portal. It prevents channel conflict and ensures partners receive appropriate credit when a deal closes.
whyWrong: Opportunity tracking is not the best choice because 'Deal Registration' is the correct answer: Partner Relationship Management is the broader category, not the specific feature name being tested here.
Lead conversion is not the best choice because lead Conversion is a Sales Cloud process, unrelated to partner deal tracking.
Partner management is not the best choice because opportunity Management alone is a general sales feature, not the partner-specific deal registration capability being asked about.

sampleQuestions.question: Who can use an Experience Cloud site, including visitors who do not sign in?
options: Only signed-in members; guest visitors are never supported
Licensed external members and permitted guest visitors
sampleQuestions.explanation: Licensed external members and permitted guest visitors is the best fit because experience Cloud supports three user types: internal Salesforce users, external authenticated users (with Customer Community, Customer Community Plus, or Partner Community licences), and guest users who access the site without logging in. Each has different object and record access capabilities.
whyWrong: Only signed-in users; guests are unsupported is not the best choice because 'Only authenticated users' contradicts the fact that guest (unauthenticated) access is explicitly supported.
Only internal Salesforce users is not the best choice because restricting to internal full-license users is the opposite of Experience Cloud's purpose, which includes external users.
Only system administrators is not the best choice because restricting to System Administrator profile contradicts the fact that a broad range of external user types can access sites.

sampleQuestions.question: What can an administrator configure with the Branding Editor?
options: Write CSS and JavaScript for every brand change
Set colors, fonts and logos without code
sampleQuestions.explanation: Set colors, fonts and logos without code is the best fit because the Branding Editor within Experience Builder allows non-technical admins to apply a consistent brand by setting primary colours, background colours, text fonts, and button styles, all via point-and-click configuration.
whyWrong: Write CSS and JavaScript for every brand change is not the best choice because the Branding Editor is specifically a no-code declarative tool, it isn't a code editor.
Review visitor analytics and demographics is not the best choice because the Branding Editor controls visual branding, it isn't an analytics panel.
Manage image files in Salesforce is not the best choice because the Branding Editor is for visual configuration, it isn't a file/asset management tool.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Salesforce feature manages structured content for publication across channels?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce CMS is the best fit because salesforce CMS is a headless content management system that enables content teams to create and publish structured content (news articles, product descriptions, banners) and deliver it to Experience Cloud sites, Marketing Cloud, and external channels via APIs.
whyWrong: Document Generation is not the best choice because chatter Groups are for collaboration, not structured multi-channel content publishing.
Chatter Groups is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Salesforce CMS.
Salesforce Knowledge is not the best choice because salesforce Knowledge manages articles but isn't the cross-channel structured content management system being described.

sampleQuestions.question: Where do administrators configure and manage Experience Cloud sites?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Experience Cloud Workspaces is the best fit because workspaces is the central administration area for Experience Cloud sites, accessible from Setup. It contains Experience Builder (visual page editor), Administration (members, login, security), Moderation, Analytics, and Content management panels.
whyWrong: A shared document space is not the best choice because a collaborative document workspace is a different concept, not what Experience Builder Workspaces provides.
A customization sandbox is not the best choice because a sandboxed testing environment is a different concept from the central admin management panel being described.
A visitor analytics dashboard is not the best choice because a reporting dashboard for traffic is a separate analytics feature, not what Experience Builder Workspaces provides.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a Lightning Bolt Solution provide for an Experience Cloud implementation?
sampleQuestions.explanation: AppExchange site package is the best fit because lightning Bolt Solutions are pre-built site packages on AppExchange created by Salesforce ISV partners. They bundle a complete site template, including pages, themes, flows, and custom components; that can be installed and configured for rapid deployment.
whyWrong: A Slack integration is not the best choice because a Lightning Component adding chat is a specific component, not the broader packaged site template concept.
A live-chat component is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as An AppExchange package with reusable site elements.
A native mobile-app builder is not the best choice because a native mobile app accelerator is a different AppExchange offering, not what a Lightning Bolt Solution is.

sampleQuestions.question: Where are permissions for unauthenticated site visitors controlled?
options: The profile shared with signed-in users
sampleQuestions.explanation: Guest User profile and sharing is the best fit because each Experience Cloud site has a dedicated Guest User profile. Admins control which objects guest users can read, which fields are visible, and which records they can access via guest user sharing rules. Salesforce has tightened guest user security in recent releases, the exam tests which access types require authentication.
whyWrong: The Minimum Access profile alone is not the best choice because guest user access isn't managed exclusively through Workspaces settings, it's controlled via the dedicated Guest User profile and sharing rules.
Workspaces settings alone is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as The site’s dedicated Guest User profile and sharing setup.
The profile shared with signed-in users is not the best choice because guest users don't share the same profile as authenticated users; they have a distinct Guest User profile.

sampleQuestions.question: How can a site display different components to members and guest visitors?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Audience visibility rules is the best fit because audience-Based Visibility in Experience Builder allows admins to define when a component or page is visible, such as showing a login prompt to guests and a personalised dashboard to authenticated members. Audiences can be based on login status, user attributes, or record data.
whyWrong: Profile-based page assignments is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as Audience-based component or page visibility.
Record page layouts is not the best choice because record Detail Page Layouts control field display on records, not member-vs-guest content differentiation.
Site.com Studio is not the best choice because site.com Studio is a legacy tool, not the current Experience Cloud mechanism for audience-based content visibility.

sampleQuestions.question: What must be configured so partner users can update the Opportunities they are allowed to access?
options: Copy partner updates into Opportunities with a custom Apex trigger
Assign a partner license and share the target Opportunities
sampleQuestions.explanation: Assign a partner license and share the target Opportunities is the best fit because partner Community licences enable external partner users to access Salesforce objects including Opportunities. Sharing must be configured, via sharing rules, sharing sets, or External Account Hierarchy, to grant access to the specific records. Guest user access cannot be used for write operations on CRM records.
whyWrong: Copy portal updates with a custom Apex trigger is not the best choice because a custom Apex trigger for syncing is unnecessary, native sharing configuration already provides this access.
Give partners internal CRM licenses is not the best choice because giving partners full internal CRM licenses is costly and unnecessary: Partner Community licenses are the purpose-built solution.

Expose Opportunities to unauthenticated visitors is not the best choice because enabling guest user access would expose Opportunity data to unauthenticated visitors, which is inappropriate for this scenario.

sampleQuestions.question: How can site members access reports and dashboards for their data?
options: CRM Analytics dashboards embedded in an iframe
sampleQuestions.explanation: Reports and dashboards with sharing is the best fit because standard Salesforce Reports and Dashboards can be made accessible in Experience Cloud sites by adding the Reports tab and configuring sharing so external users see only their own data. For more advanced analytics, CRM Analytics can be embedded within site pages.
whyWrong: CRM Analytics in an iframe only is not the best choice because chatter Feed analytics tracks post engagement, not general business reporting.
Chatter engagement metrics is not the best choice because salesforce CMS publishing metrics track content performance, not general business reports/dashboards.
CMS publishing metrics is not the best choice because it does not meet the scenario as directly as External-user access to Reports and Dashboards, with sharing configured.

sampleQuestions.question: What access pattern do Sharing Sets use for external users?
options: Set site colors, logos and other visual branding
Share Salesforce Files with authenticated internal employees
Match records to an external user’s Account or Contact
Grant site members access to available reports and dashboards
sampleQuestions.explanation: Match records to an external user’s Account or Contact is the best fit because Sharing Sets use configured Account or Contact mappings to grant external-user record access.
whyWrong: Set site colors, logos and other visual branding is not the best choice because branding changes appearance, not record access.
Share Salesforce Files with authenticated internal employees is not the best choice because internal file sharing does not grant external users access to related records.
Grant site members access to available reports and dashboards is not the best choice because dashboard access does not control which underlying records an external user can access.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants prospective customers to create their own portal account without an admin manually adding each one. What should the consultant configure?
options: A self-registration page for the site
Manually create a new Contact for every visitor
A single shared login for every customer
sampleQuestions.explanation: A self-registration page lets prospects create their own account, which then creates the underlying Contact and User automatically, without manual admin work per person.
whyWrong: Manually creating a Contact for every visitor doesn't scale and defeats the purpose of self-service signup.
Disabling guest access would prevent anyone from reaching the registration page in the first place.
A single shared login would prevent tracking individual customers and their own data access.

sampleQuestions.question: A company wants employees to sign into an Experience Cloud site using their existing corporate identity provider credentials, not a separate Salesforce password. What should the consultant set up?
options: An authentication provider or SSO configuration for the site
A stricter password policy applied to the site's member profile
A sharing set that grants access to related records
sampleQuestions.explanation: Configuring an authentication provider or SSO lets users log in with their existing corporate identity provider credentials instead of a separate Salesforce-specific login.
whyWrong: A password policy still relies on a separate Salesforce login, it doesn't enable SSO with an external identity provider.
A Sharing Set controls record access, it has nothing to do with how a user authenticates.
A Content Workspace organizes CMS content, unrelated to authentication.

sampleQuestions.question: A client wants a highly specific, non-standard interaction on their site that no out-of-the-box Experience Builder component supports. What should the consultant consider, and what should they check first?
options: A custom Lightning web component, after confirming it fits within Experience Cloud's customization limits
A full rebuild of the site on another platform, after confirming the budget with the client's sponsor
sampleQuestions.explanation: Custom LWCs can extend Experience Builder beyond standard components, but a consultant should first check documented customization considerations and limitations before committing to a design.
whyWrong: Declaring it impossible without checking custom component options skips a real, available solution.
Rebuilding outside Salesforce abandons the platform unnecessarily for a solvable requirement.
Ignoring a stated requirement isn't a valid consulting response.

sampleQuestions.question: A site owner wants to see how many members are actively logging in and engaging with content each month. What should they review?
options: Experience Cloud site analytics and dashboards
The Branding Editor's theme and colour settings panel
sampleQuestions.explanation: Site analytics and dashboards track member login and engagement trends, which is exactly what Adoption and Analytics covers.
whyWrong: The Branding Editor controls visual appearance, not engagement tracking.
A Sharing Set controls record access, not usage analytics.
A Content Type defines a kind of CMS content, it doesn't report on member activity.

sampleQuestions.question: A business wants a lightweight, simple landing page experience rather than a full-featured portal with cases and knowledge. Which template type best fits?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Microsite template is designed for lightweight landing pages, not the full case-and-knowledge feature set of a support-focused template.
whyWrong: Customer Service (Napili) is built around case deflection and support, more than a simple landing page needs.
Partner Central is designed for partner relationship management, not a simple public landing page.
Help Centre is a self-service knowledge template, heavier than a simple landing page requirement.
